items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Interviewer mentions Chuck Berry; Interviewee responds by discussing studio musicians copying Elvis and later comparing early rock 'n roll rhythm sections to early bebop, without stating any personal interaction with Chuck Berry.

ctx.x: We all played it. We were all doing record dates that were trying to copy Elvis Presley and all the other, well I don’t know is Elvis Presley rock ‘n roll? I guess.
He was for a while. And Chuck Berry and those guys.

We all — studio musicians were expected to play everything and I found that I could fit into that kind of stuff because I knew how to play boogie woogie and blues piano from my big brother’s record collection. I played a lot of stuff for Atlantic Records — Jerry Wexler and —
